title: How To Think Like A Strategic Genius (5-Dimensional Thinking)

sentences.en: Some of the smartest people I know are incredibly stupid, and some of the dumbest people that I know are incredibly successful by today's standards.
sentences.zh: 我认识的一些最聪明的人，蠢得离谱；而我认识的一些最笨的人，按今天的标准来看，成功得离谱。

sentences.en: They're happy, they're healthy, they're wealthy.
sentences.zh: 他们快乐、健康、富有。

sentences.en: So what's actually going on here?
sentences.zh: 所以到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Why are smart, intelligent people who tend to overanalyze a lot of things, not achieve the life they want because in this video, I'm trying to prove to you that thinking is one of the most important things that you can practice in today's world.
sentences.zh: 为什么那些聪明、高智商、凡事过度分析的人，反而过不上自己想要的生活？因为在这个视频里，我想向你证明：思考，是你在当今世界能练习的最重要的事之一。

sentences.en: Thinking is the one thing that determines the outcome of your life, and that's massive.
sentences.zh: 思考是决定你人生结果的唯一因素，这分量极重。

sentences.en: The outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 你人生的结果。

sentences.en: That's literally everything.
sentences.zh: 那真的就是一切。

sentences.en: So if you learn how to think, which is what we're going to learn here, but we're not going to do it in a way where we talk about first principles thinking or systems thinking or metacognition or anything else that you can ask ChatGPT about, because that's why you're here.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你学会如何思考——这就是我们要学的内容——但我们不会去讲第一性原理、系统思维、元认知，或者任何你可以问 ChatGPT 的东西，因为那不是你来这里的原因。

sentences.en: You're here for a unique take.
sentences.zh: 你来这里是为了一个独特的视角。

sentences.en: Now, I've spent multiple years studying different thinkers, and I've spent a lot of time dissecting how they think and trying to integrate that into my own way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几年研究不同的思想家，花了很多时间剖析他们的思考方式，并试图融入我自己的思考方式里。

sentences.en: So what we're going to do in this video is we're going to start very shallow and build our way up.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个视频里，我们要从很浅的地方开始，一步步往上搭建。

sentences.en: We're going to start at one dimensional thinking, then two dimensional, then three dimensional, then four dimensional, and finally we're going to go we're going to tap into the fifth dimension.
sentences.zh: 我们从一维思考开始，然后二维，然后三维，然后四维，最后我们要触达第五维度。

sentences.en: So thinking tip number one if you want to understand what something is like thinking or genius thinking, it helps to understand the opposite, to understand what stupid thinking is.
sentences.zh: 所以思考建议第一条：如果你想理解某样东西是什么，比如思考或天才式思考，理解它的反面会很有帮助，也就是理解什么是愚蠢的思考。

sentences.en: And when I say stupid thinking here, I'm not calling you stupid.
sentences.zh: 我在这里说愚蠢的思考，不是在骂你蠢。

sentences.en: I'm not calling you low IQ.
sentences.zh: 不是在说你智商低。

sentences.en: I'm simply observing a pattern.
sentences.zh: 我只是在观察一种模式。

sentences.en: Everyone thinks stupidly at times, everyone thinks stupidly every single day. And that's what we're trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会有愚蠢思考的时候，每个人每一天都在愚蠢地思考。而我们要做的，就是避免这一点。

sentences.en: That's what we're trying to move in the direction away from.
sentences.zh: 我们要做的，就是朝远离它的方向前进。

sentences.en: I can't think right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在没法思考。

sentences.en: So if we observe people who display this characteristic of stupid thinking, we come away with a few insights.
sentences.zh: 如果我们观察那些表现出愚蠢思考特征的人，我们会得出几条洞见。

sentences.en: First is that stupid thinking is one dimensional.
sentences.zh: 第一，愚蠢的思考是一维的。

sentences.en: People try to jam everything into their own perspective and have difficulty seeing outside of it.
sentences.zh: 人们试图把所有东西都塞进自己的视角里，很难看到视角之外的东西。

sentences.en: Second, stupid thinking is reductionistic.
sentences.zh: 第二，愚蠢的思考是简化主义的。

sentences.en: So experts in one domain like business try to reduce everything to a strategy problem as one example.
sentences.zh: 比如，某个领域的专家，比如商业领域，倾向于把所有问题都简化成一个策略问题。

sentences.en: Third, stupid thinking is tribal.
sentences.zh: 第三，愚蠢的思考是部落式的。

sentences.en: So you only trust your group, your political party, your tribe, your religious people who adopt your same religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 你只信任你的群体、你的政党、你的部落、和你信仰相同宗教的人。

sentences.en: Then you consider everyone else wrong because they don't conform and forth.
sentences.zh: 然后你认为其他所有人都是错的，因为他们不顺从。第四——

sentences.en: Stupid thinking does not question your justification for most things is that's just how it's done.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢的思考不会质疑。你对大多数事情的辩解就是：事情就是这么做的。

sentences.en: So as a whole, stupid thinking is about closing your mind off once you've reached the limits of what you know.
sentences.zh: 所以整体来看，愚蠢的思考就是：一旦触及你认知的边界，就把大脑关掉。

sentences.en: Stupid thinking is when you stop thinking too early, you can still think within your own little bubble, but you never break out of that bubble.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢的思考就是过早停止思考。你仍然可以在自己的小泡泡里思考，但你永远不会打破那个泡泡。

sentences.en: What tends to happen is you think for a bit, but then you reach a point where you're at your limits of how far you can think, and then you tend to collapse in on what you know.
sentences.zh: 通常发生的情况是，你思考了一会儿，然后到达了你思考能力的极限，接着你就坍缩回你已知的东西里。

sentences.en: And then that's when you just become this person who just spews out preprogramed thoughts, or what they've been told, or what other people believe is right.
sentences.zh: 然后你就变成了那种人：只会吐出预先编程好的想法，或者别人告诉他们的东西，或者别人认为对的东西。

sentences.en: They don't push the boundaries of their own mind.
sentences.zh: 他们不去推自己思维的边界。

sentences.en: So with that, as an explanation of stupid thinking, we can start to grasp at what genius thinking could be.
sentences.zh: 有了这些对愚蠢思考的解释，我们就可以开始去理解天才式思考可能是什么了。

sentences.en: In this case, genius thinking as a definition would be the ability to hold threatening ideas in the realm of possibility, paired with the intention to understand rather than just know the mark of genius.
sentences.zh: 在这个语境下，天才思维的定义是：能够将具有威胁性的想法保留在可能性领域内，同时带着理解的意图，而非仅仅知道——这才是天才的标志。

sentences.en: Thinking is illustrated by the width, depth, and height at which you can think without being cut off from venturing further, often due to holding an idea as absolute.
sentences.zh: 思维的标志，在于你能在宽度、深度和高度上思考到什么程度，而不会因为把某个想法视为绝对真理，就被切断继续探索的可能。

sentences.en: It's your ability to traverse the full universal web of ideas, reality, or all potential knowledge and pull them together into something coherent or useful, if not something entirely new.
sentences.zh: 是你穿越整个关于想法、现实或所有潜在知识的宇宙网络，并将它们整合成某种连贯、有用的东西——甚至是全新东西的能力。

sentences.en: But this also helps us see what this smart but dumb phenomenon is, where someone very smart in a domain like business will see someone who is depressed and just attribute that to being a productivity issue.
sentences.zh: 但这也能帮我们看清那个"聪明但愚蠢"的现象：一个在商业等领域非常聪明的人，看到一个抑郁的人，只会把它归结为生产力问题。

sentences.en: Or dude, you just need to sit down and do the work.
sentences.zh: 或者"兄弟，你只需要坐下来干活就行了。"

sentences.en: You see this everywhere on social media.
sentences.zh: 你在社交媒体上到处都能看到这种论调。

sentences.en: If you're depressed, just do the work.
sentences.zh: 如果你抑郁了，干活就行。

sentences.en: If you're sad, just do the work.
sentences.zh: 如果你难过了，干活就行。

sentences.en: And in some cases that helps.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下这确实有用。

sentences.en: But it doesn't help. In every case.
sentences.zh: 但它不是在所有情况下都有用。

sentences.en: It's like you're a little kid and you're trying to take the circle shape and you're trying to like, mash it into the square shape and the little board.
sentences.zh: 就像你是个小孩，拿着一个圆形积木，拼命想把它塞进那个方形的孔里。

sentences.en: And the same holds true for the other side, right?
sentences.zh: 反过来也是一样，对吧？

sentences.en: There's like business person who's very practical, and then there's a spiritual person who's very abstract, and the spiritual person would attribute business failure to just not having the right vibration.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常务实的商人，还有一个非常抽象的通灵者，那个通灵者会把商业失败归结为"你的振动频率不对"。

sentences.en: And the thing here is, is that they're both not wrong.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，他们俩都没错。

sentences.en: They're both correct in their own ways.
sentences.zh: 他们各自在自己的体系里都是对的。

sentences.en: But we have to understand how to apply those ways of thinking to different situations so that we can get the most out of it.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须理解如何把这些思维方式应用到不同的情境中，才能从中获得最大收益。

sentences.en: Because wouldn't it help as a business person, if you had a problem that you couldn't see, because it's best solved through something spiritual?
sentences.zh: 因为作为一个商人，如果你有一个看不见的问题，而它恰恰最适合用某种灵性方式来解决，那能切换到那个视角去真正解决问题，不是很好吗？

sentences.en: To be able to tap into that lens so that you can actually solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 能够接入那个透镜，让你真正解决问题。

sentences.en: So you've met these people, you've met these business people who just prescribe their way of doing things as the only way of doing things.
sentences.zh: 你遇到过这些人，你遇到过那些把自己的做事方式规定为唯一方式的商人。

sentences.en: You've met the hippies and the spiritual people who do the same thing, and you probably do the same thing without noticing it.
sentences.zh: 你遇到过那些做同样事情的嬉皮士和灵性人士，而你自己很可能也在做同样的事，只是没注意到。

sentences.en: And that's what I'm trying to get at here, is that if if you just notice that if you simply notice it and don't allow your thinking to stop there, then you unlock this new power.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想说的：如果你只是注意到它，如果你只是注意到它，并且不让你的思维停在那里，你就会解锁一种新的力量。

sentences.en: So how do we actually start navigating out of stupid thinking?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何真正开始走出愚蠢思维？

sentences.en: The first thing that will help here is just knowing the difference between knowing and understanding.
sentences.zh: 这里第一个有帮助的东西，就是知道"知道"和"理解"之间的区别。

sentences.en: Now, this isn't an explicit definition.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个精确的定义。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to get you to understand here, which is kind of ironic, but knowing we can think of that as horizontal development, it's domain expertise.
sentences.zh: 我只是想让你理解这一点——说起来有点讽刺——"知道"，我们可以把它看作横向发展，是领域专长。

sentences.en: You're accumulating facts, you're memorizing insights, you're studying the textbook.
sentences.zh: 你在积累事实，你在记忆洞见，你在研读教科书。

sentences.en: You know things and understanding is vertical.
sentences.zh: 你知道很多东西。而"理解"是纵向的。

sentences.en: It's it has more to do with the sophistication of your cognitive operating system.
sentences.zh: 它更多与你认知操作系统的精密程度有关。

sentences.en: So you can know a lot and understand very little.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以知道很多，但理解很少。

sentences.en: You can also understand deeply and know relatively little.
sentences.zh: 你也可以理解很深，但知道得相对较少。

sentences.en: But if you understand more than you know, you can still act more effectively than the person who thinks they know everything.
sentences.zh: 但如果你理解得比你知道的多，你仍然可以比那些自以为无所不知的人行动得更有效。

sentences.en: And that's exactly why smart people are stuck, is they read books, they collect knowledge, they develop themselves this way, but they can't see anything above that.
sentences.zh: 这正是聪明人被困住的原因：他们读书，收集知识，用这种方式发展自己，但他们看不到那之上的任何东西。

sentences.en: They can't see into other domains.
sentences.zh: 他们看不到其他领域。

sentences.en: It's like they're installing new apps onto their operating system without upgrading the operating system itself.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在自己的操作系统上安装新应用，却没有升级操作系统本身。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When you have an old iPhone and you download a new app, that app is probably going to be very slow.
sentences.zh: 你拿一台老 iPhone 去下载一个新 App，那个 App 大概率会非常卡。

sentences.en: It's not going to work very well.
sentences.zh: 根本跑不顺。

sentences.en: A lot of the features are developed for the newer operating system.
sentences.zh: 很多功能是为新系统开发的。

sentences.en: So when it comes to your own mind, you have to do the same.
sentences.zh: 所以回到你自己的大脑，你得做同样的事。

sentences.en: So a few more examples of the smart but dumb phenomenon is like think of a business man, very successful in business, but he still finds himself unhappy, right?
sentences.zh: 再举几个"聪明但愚蠢"的例子——想想一个商人，生意上非常成功，但他还是觉得自己不快乐，对吧？

sentences.en: He makes $100 million and he sells the company, and now he's depressed and he doesn't know how to solve that problem because he's not in business anymore.
sentences.zh: 他赚了 1 亿美元，把公司卖了，然后抑郁了，他不知道怎么解决这个问题，因为他已经不在生意场上了。

sentences.en: And that's all he knows.
sentences.zh: 而那就是他唯一懂的东西。

sentences.en: Or, and I'm sure many of you can relate with this is a creative who has very beautiful work.
sentences.zh: 或者——我相信很多人能感同身受——一个创作者，作品非常漂亮。

sentences.en: They dedicated their lives to their craft, but when it comes time to make an income, they can't because they don't understand anything in the business domain or even in the psychological domain, and how humans perceive value because they're not creating something that other people want.
sentences.zh: 他们把一生奉献给了自己的手艺，但到了要赚钱的时候，他们做不到，因为他们对商业领域一无所知，甚至对心理学领域、对人类如何感知价值也一无所知，因为他们没有在创造别人想要的东西。

sentences.en: And that's not inherently a problem, but it can create problems, because if you want to do that thing full time and you're working a job, or you're trying to scrape by time to actually work on your creative craft, that's kind of a problem.
sentences.zh: 这本身不是问题，但它会制造问题，因为如果你想全职做那件事，而你还在打工，或者你在拼命挤时间来做你的创作，这就有问题了。

sentences.en: You want to spend all of your time doing the creative thing, but you're not willing to learn what's going to allow you to do that because you think everything just boils down to, oh, I just want to be able to create art all day.
sentences.zh: 你想把所有时间都花在创作上，但你又不愿意去学那些能让你做到这一点的东西，因为你认为一切都可以归结为——哦，我只想整天搞创作。

sentences.en: Why can't I create art all day?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不能整天搞创作？

sentences.en: And then another example is like a meat head who is very fit or goes to the gym, but their relationship is in shambles because they don't understand social dynamics.
sentences.zh: 再举一个例子——一个肌肉男，身材很好，天天去健身房，但他的感情生活一团糟，因为他不懂社交动态。

sentences.en: They haven't studied masculine feminine dynamics, they don't understand any of that.
sentences.zh: 他没研究过两性动态，他完全不懂这些。

sentences.en: So they got buff for the sake of attracting a girl, but then they can't keep it and they don't know how to solve it because all they understand is, oh, if I get buff girls like me.
sentences.zh: 所以他练壮是为了吸引女生，但他留不住，他也不知道怎么解决，因为他唯一懂的就是——哦，只要我练壮了，女生就会喜欢我。

sentences.en: So that's why learning how to think is so important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么学会如何思考如此重要。

sentences.en: Because your mind is how you interact with reality.
sentences.zh: 因为你的大脑是你与现实互动的方式。

sentences.en: You process information, you make sense of it, which is thinking.
sentences.zh: 你处理信息，你理解信息，这就是思考。

sentences.en: You make a choice.
sentences.zh: 你做出选择。

sentences.en: Then you receive information as feedback.
sentences.zh: 然后你收到信息作为反馈。

sentences.en: So you have to think again, and you respond to that feedback and repeat the cycle so you get information you think make a choice.
sentences.zh: 于是你必须再次思考，你回应那个反馈，重复这个循环——你得到信息，你思考，你做出选择。

sentences.en: You get information back from the choice.
sentences.zh: 你从选择中得到反馈信息。

sentences.en: You think. You make another choice.
sentences.zh: 你思考。你做出另一个选择。

sentences.en: You do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你做同样的事。

sentences.en: Think information choice.
sentences.zh: 思考、信息、选择。

sentences.en: Repeat, repeat, repeat.
sentences.zh: 重复、重复、重复。

sentences.en: Thinking determines the outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 思考决定你人生的结果。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: So every moment where you engage in stupid thinking creates a compounding effect.
sentences.zh: 所以，每一个你进行愚蠢思考的时刻，都会产生复利效应。

sentences.en: You dig yourself into this rut so deep that it's it becomes impossible to even see the thing that will get you out.
sentences.zh: 你把自己挖进一个深坑，深到连那条能把你拉出来的路都看不见了。

sentences.en: So the more you double down on what you know as the one true way and you fail to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以你越是加倍押注在你已知的"唯一正确道路"上，你就越学不进去。

sentences.en: Learning is kind of like an expansion pack for your thinking, right?
sentences.zh: 学习就像是给你的思考装一个扩展包，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you continue to learn and I'm not talking about studying or memorizing facts, I'm talking about how to actually learn, which is by building projects, failing, getting feedback, repeating, iterating, doing it in the real world.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你持续学习——我说的不是死记硬背或者背事实，我说的是真正学会如何学习，也就是通过构建项目、失败、获得反馈、重复、迭代，在真实世界里去做。

sentences.en: That's how you make your life better.
sentences.zh: 这就是让你的人生变得更好的方式。

sentences.en: So let's break this down into an actual framework.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来把它拆解成一个实际的框架。

sentences.en: And we're going to call this lines levels and altitudes.
sentences.zh: 我们把它叫做线、层级和高度。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So first dimension second dimension third dimension of thinking.
sentences.zh: 第一维度、第二维度、第三维度的思考。

sentences.en: And we'll just move up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 我们顺着阶梯往上走。

sentences.en: So we'll start with lines of thinking.
sentences.zh: 先从思考的线开始。

sentences.en: So here's a graphic of how this will start to look.
sentences.zh: 这是它看起来大概的样子。

sentences.en: You can think of the width of this the novice to advanced as one line of thinking. Right.
sentences.zh: 你可以把从新手到高阶的这个宽度，看作一条思考的线。

sentences.en: You can think of this entire thing as you learning, let's say marketing or astrophysics or politics or social dynamics or, religion, literally learning anything.
sentences.zh: 你可以把整件事看作你在学习，比如营销、天体物理、政治、社会动力学、宗教，学任何东西。

sentences.en: It's when you attempt to learn domain specific knowledge, this graph applies to one domain, and you are increasing the width of that line of thinking.
sentences.zh: 当你试图学习某个领域的知识时，这张图对应一个领域，而你正在拓宽那条思考的线。

sentences.en: It's like you're gaining experience in a video game.
sentences.zh: 就像你在电子游戏里积累经验值。

sentences.en: Now. Levels.
sentences.zh: 接下来，层级。

sentences.en: On the other hand, how these are stacked is how you think about each line.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，它们如何堆叠，就是你如何看待每一条线。

sentences.en: And we've talked about how cognitive development evolves over time many times before see can Wilbur see Susan Cook Reuters see Spiral Dynamics, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们之前聊过很多次认知发展如何随时间演化，参考 Ken Wilber、Susan Cook-Greuter、螺旋动力学等等。

sentences.en: But we can extract those patterns and apply them to thinking itself about specific domains and multiple domains.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以提取那些模式，把它们应用到思考本身，无论是针对单一领域还是多个领域。

sentences.en: So at level zero of thinking it's instinctual.
sentences.zh: 在思考的第零层，是本能。

sentences.en: So you're just born right?
sentences.zh: 你刚出生，对吧？

sentences.en: When you're born you just act out of pure survival.
sentences.zh: 你出生时，行为纯粹出于生存本能。

sentences.en: You react to stimulus without thinking at all.
sentences.zh: 你对刺激做出反应，完全不思考。

sentences.en: You don't even have the ability to think.
sentences.zh: 你甚至没有思考的能力。

sentences.en: And then level one is conformist.
sentences.zh: 然后第一层是从众。

sentences.en: So this is black and white thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是非黑即白的思考。

sentences.en: You follow rules and obey authority without questioning.
sentences.zh: 你遵守规则、服从权威，不加质疑。

sentences.en: You adopt others perspective.
sentences.zh: 你采纳他人的视角。

sentences.en: So when you're born, you adopt your parents perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以你出生时，采纳父母的视角。

sentences.en: You take on their religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 你接受他们的宗教信仰。

sentences.en: You take on what they think you should do for a career.
sentences.zh: 你接受他们认为你该做什么职业。

sentences.en: And if they're born in the industrial age, that equals go to school, get a job, retire at 65.
sentences.zh: 如果他们出生在工业时代，那就等于上学、找工作、65岁退休。

sentences.en: And then there's level two, which is the individualist stage where critical thinking emerges and you construct your own model.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二层，个体主义阶段，批判性思维出现，你开始构建自己的模型。

sentences.en: So you build your own perspective.
sentences.zh: 你建立自己的视角。

sentences.en: And for a lot of people, this is often based on their parents perspective.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这通常还是基于父母的视角。

sentences.en: They don't fully break out yet they they are still in this singular, one dimensional way of thinking about the world.
sentences.zh: 他们还没完全挣脱，仍然陷在一种单一的、一维的看待世界的方式里。

sentences.en: So you may not do exactly what your parents want you to do, but you're still on the default path that society set for you.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能不会完全按父母说的做，但你仍然走在社会为你设定的默认路径上。

sentences.en: So go to school, get a job, retire at 65, and you may be choosing your own major.
sentences.zh: 所以上学、找工作、65岁退休，你可能确实选了自己的专业。

sentences.en: You may how you may want to get an art degree when your parents disagree with that, but they're still happy that you're going to college to get a degree.
sentences.zh: 你可能想读艺术学位而你父母不同意，但他们依然很高兴你上了大学、拿了个学位。

sentences.en: And then there's level three, which I'm going to call synthesis.
sentences.zh: 然后是第三层，我称之为"融合"。

sentences.en: And this is where you see your model as one among many.
sentences.zh: 在这一层，你把自己的模型看作众多模型中的一个。

sentences.en: You hold contradictions and use perspectives as tools rather than law or someone questionable truth.
sentences.zh: 你容纳矛盾，把视角当作工具，而不是铁律或某个人可疑的真理。

sentences.en: Now, these aren't just things that I've made up.
sentences.zh: 这些不是我瞎编的。

sentences.en: This is how minds evolve over time.
sentences.zh: 这就是心智随时间演化的方式。

sentences.en: This has been documented in a lot of people don't reach that level three.
sentences.zh: 这已经被记录下来了，而很多人达不到第三层。

sentences.en: They either remain Bible thumpers, so to say, across multiple domains, not just religion as level one thinkers where they rebel against that and consider their own way of doing things as law.
sentences.zh: 他们要么停留在"圣经狂热者"状态——这么说吧，跨越多个领域，不只是宗教——作为第一层思考者；要么他们反抗这一点，然后把自己做事的方式当成铁律。

sentences.en: But when you're a synthesis, you start to break out of the like single minded perspective.
sentences.zh: 但当你是一个融合者时，你开始打破那种单一视角。

sentences.en: You start to understand that, oh, there is actually some form of truth in how other people do things, which is a crazy thought to many people who knew that everyone is right in one way or another.
sentences.zh: 你开始理解，哦，别人做事的方式里其实也有某种形式的真理，这对很多人来说是个疯狂的想法——谁会想到每个人在某个层面上都是对的。

sentences.en: And then level four, we're going to call this generative thinking.
sentences.zh: 然后是第四层，我们称之为"生成性思考"。

sentences.en: So you create original perspectives that didn't exist before, or you come to ideas without outside influence.
sentences.zh: 你创造出以前不存在的原创视角，或者你在没有外部影响的情况下得出想法。

sentences.en: So if we go back to the graph, you can see how like level one starts to unlock level two and then level three and then level four.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回到那个图表，你可以看到第一层如何开始解锁第二层，然后第三层，然后第四层。

sentences.en: It's not like you have to get 100% through level one in order to move up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 不是说你要把第一层100%走完才能往上爬。

sentences.en: Like you can be at level one completely, but you can tap into level four occasionally.
sentences.zh: 你可以完全处于第一层，但偶尔也能触达第四层。

sentences.en: But of course we want to tap into that more.
sentences.zh: 但我们当然想更多地触达它。

sentences.en: We want to maximize this so that we increase our surface area of thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们想最大化这一点，以扩大我们的思考表面积。

sentences.en: Now one important distinction here is that level one and level two can be considered first tier thinking.
sentences.zh: 这里一个重要的区分是，第一层和第二层可以被视为第一梯队思考。

sentences.en: If we group those together, what that means is that it's overly dogmatic.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把它们归为一组，这意味着它是过度教条的。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I'm right, you're wrong, or my group is right.
sentences.zh: 我是对的，你是错的，或者我的群体是对的。

sentences.en: Your group is wrong.
sentences.zh: 你的群体是错的。

sentences.en: And then they fight against each other a lot.
sentences.zh: 然后它们彼此之间大量对抗。

sentences.en: Then level three and levels four can be considered second tier thinking.
sentences.zh: 而第三层和第四层可以被视为第二梯队思考。

sentences.en: This is where you start to reject dogma and you start to actually seek truth for once, because your truth isn't the only truth.
sentences.zh: 在这里你开始拒绝教条，你开始真正地——哪怕一次——去寻求真理，因为你的真理不是唯一的真理。

sentences.en: You understand that the ultimate truth lies somewhere in the middle, and usually you don't come to absolute truth.
sentences.zh: 你理解终极真理存在于中间的某个地方，而且通常你不会得出绝对真理。

sentences.en: You come to trade offs, right?
sentences.zh: 你得出的是权衡取舍，对吧？

sentences.en: Solutions like solutions don't really exist, but trade offs do. That's Thomas rule.
sentences.zh: 解决方案——解决方案并不真正存在，但权衡取舍存在。这是托马斯·索维尔说的。

sentences.en: Now one more thing here is that you can be at level four, but in a particularly stressful situation you can regress back down into lower levels.
sentences.zh: 还有一点是，你可能处于第四层，但在一个特别有压力的情况下，你会退回到更低的层次。

sentences.en: So you can regress down to level one and be very conformist in one domain of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会退回到第一层，在你生活的某个领域变得非常顺从。

sentences.en: When you're stressed and you're going through it, or you're in an argument with someone and you're really not thinking, that's when you start to like tap into the lower levels.
sentences.zh: 当你压力很大、正在经历困境，或者你在跟人争吵、真的没有在思考的时候，那就是你开始触达更低层次的时候。

sentences.en: So before we continue, I just want to make this exceedingly clear once again, is that genius level thinking is your ability to continue thinking, because at each level of thinking, your ability to navigate that space to both known and unknown ideas continues to expand.
sentences.zh: 所以在继续之前，我想再次把这一点说得极其清楚：天才级别的思考，是你持续思考的能力，因为在每一个思考层次上，你驾驭那个空间——既包括已知也包括未知的想法——的能力都在持续扩展。

sentences.en: When you're born, you don't really think when you're a conformist or level one.
sentences.zh: 当你出生时，你并不真正思考；当你是一个顺从者或处于第一层时，你也不真正思考。

sentences.en: You think until you reach a point where you have the answer.
sentences.zh: 你一直思考，直到得出一个答案。

sentences.en: Then you start defending the answer.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始捍卫那个答案。

sentences.en: When you're an individualist or level two, you do the same thing, but with your answer.
sentences.zh: 当你成为个人主义者，也就是第二层时，你做同样的事，只不过捍卫的是你自己的答案。

sentences.en: And when you reach synthesis, you can think far and wide, but your ability to create new lines of thought is not fully developed yet.
sentences.zh: 当你达到综合阶段，你可以想得很广很远，但你创造新思路的能力还没有完全发展出来。

sentences.en: So reaching your highest ability to think and thus providing the runway for your highest potential in this life boils down to the simple practice of noticing when your mind feels threatened, being honest with yourself, and, at minimum, staying open to new perspectives.
sentences.zh: 所以，要达到你最高的思考能力，从而为你此生最高的潜力铺好跑道，归根结底是一个简单的练习：觉察到你的头脑什么时候感到威胁，对自己诚实，至少保持对新视角的开放。

sentences.en: That's thinking in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 这就是思考的核心。

sentences.en: That's how you think.
sentences.zh: 这就是你思考的方式。

sentences.en: You don't need any fancy first principles.
sentences.zh: 你不需要任何花哨的第一性原理。

sentences.en: Thinking to do that, even though first principles thinking holds some truths.
sentences.zh: 用不着那些，尽管第一性原理思考确实包含一些真理。

sentences.en: Now, after lines and levels of thinking, there is your altitude of thinking.
sentences.zh: 好，在思考的线和层级之后，还有思考的高度。

sentences.en: What is the average of how you think about each line or level?
sentences.zh: 你对每一条线、每一个层级的思考，平均水平是什么样的？

sentences.en: So if we look at a new graph, you can kind of see I've condensed the lines, I've added more domains, and now they're interconnected and you're at various different levels.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看一张新图，你会看到我把那些线压缩了，增加了更多领域，现在它们相互连接，你处在不同的层级上。

sentences.en: And you may see something that you've seen before here.
sentences.zh: 你可能会在这里看到一些你以前见过的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: To best understand how this works and to almost complete the thinking puzzle, it helps to visualize thinking as a skill tree.
sentences.zh: 要最好地理解这是如何运作的，并几乎完成这个思考拼图，把思考想象成一棵技能树会很有帮助。

sentences.en: So in a video game, you can put points into certain traits that allow you to do more.
sentences.zh: 在电子游戏里，你可以把点数分配到某些特质上，让你能做更多事情。

sentences.en: Inside the game, you can take on higher challenges, you can have more fun and you can continue playing.
sentences.zh: 在游戏里，你可以接受更高的挑战，获得更多乐趣，继续玩下去。

sentences.en: The same holds true with the mind.
sentences.zh: 头脑也是一样的道理。

sentences.en: But the thing is here, higher level traits can only be unlocked once you meet a specific requirement of lower level traits.
sentences.zh: 但这里的关键是，更高层级的特质只有在满足低层级特质的特定要求后才能解锁。

sentences.en: So in a video game, you can't access something like level three dexterity when you haven't already put enough points into, let's say, level three strength.
sentences.zh: 在游戏里，如果你没有在比如说三级力量上投入足够的点数，你就无法解锁三级敏捷之类的东西。

sentences.en: So many of you are interested in business, which is why I keep bringing this up as an example.
sentences.zh: 你们很多人对商业感兴趣，这也是我为什么一直拿它举例。

sentences.en: But imagine a business person who takes it pretty far, right?
sentences.zh: 想象一个把事业做得相当远的商人，对吧？

sentences.en: You make a lot of money, but then you hit this plateau and you're like, man, I don't know what to do here.
sentences.zh: 你赚了很多钱，但然后你撞上了瓶颈，你会想，天哪，我不知道该怎么办了。

sentences.en: Like, I literally don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: I've studied everything and I can't overcome this plateau.
sentences.zh: 我什么都学过了，就是突破不了这个瓶颈。

sentences.en: And you can't see the problem because you haven't developed other domains of your life.
sentences.zh: 你看不到问题所在，因为你没有发展生活的其他领域。

sentences.en: The problem here could be your inability to lead a team, right?
sentences.zh: 这里的问题可能是你无法领导一个团队，对吧？

sentences.en: Your emotional intelligence is so abysmally low that you don't even know that you're causing problems within the company that's causing it to stall in order to be a true leader, you have to develop yourself in all domains of life.
sentences.zh: 你的情商低得可怜，你甚至不知道自己正在公司内部制造问题，导致公司停滞不前。要成为一个真正的领导者，你必须在生活的所有领域发展自己。

sentences.en: At least that's my belief.
sentences.zh: 至少这是我的信念。

sentences.en: And even if there are people who make it very high without doing that, other domains of their life suffer as well.
sentences.zh: 即使有人不这么做也爬得很高，他们生活的其他领域同样会遭殃。

sentences.en: That's not something that I want, at least right now in my life.
sentences.zh: 那不是我想要的，至少在我人生的这个阶段不是。

sentences.en: I want to help you have one life.
sentences.zh: 我想帮你拥有一个完整的人生。

sentences.en: Maybe, I don't know, maybe I changes that.
sentences.zh: 也许，我不知道，也许我会改变这个想法。

sentences.en: But I want to do cool things in this life.
sentences.zh: 但我想在这一生中做一些很酷的事。

sentences.en: I don't want to let problems sit around and fester and just make my life worse.
sentences.zh: 我不想让问题搁在那儿发烂，把我的生活越搞越糟。

sentences.en: This is also why domains like politics or religion or even things like nutrition online are so like violent and polarizing.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么像政治、宗教，甚至网上的营养学这类领域，会那么激烈、那么两极分化。

sentences.en: It's a bunch of smart but dumb people just calling each other idiots because they can't see from each other's perspective.
sentences.zh: 就是一群聪明但愚蠢的人互相骂白痴，因为他们根本看不到对方的视角。

sentences.en: Okay, so now we need to tap into the fourth dimension.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在我们要进入第四个维度了。

sentences.en: We covered wine's levels and altitude, but now there's something more.
sentences.zh: 我们讲了 Wine 的层级和高度，但现在还有更多东西。

sentences.en: Now this isn't the fourth dimension of time.
sentences.zh: 这个不是时间的第四维度。

sentences.en: That's actually the fifth dimension that we're going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 那其实是我们接下来要讲的第五维度。

sentences.en: But this fourth dimension does increase your ability to think by the power of four, because there are four dimensions of reality, and these dimensions are perspectives.
sentences.zh: 但这个第四维度确实能把你的思考能力提升四次方，因为现实有四个维度，而这些维度就是视角。

sentences.en: They're ways of looking at the world in four different major ways.
sentences.zh: 它们是四种截然不同的看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: So when you're thinking about a belief or an idea or a situation or problem, you can kind of adjust the lens on your camera to see it in four different ways.
sentences.zh: 所以当你在思考一个信念、一个想法、一个处境或一个问题时，你可以调整你相机上的镜头，用四种不同的方式去看它。

sentences.en: So here's how this would look in graphic form.
sentences.zh: 用图形来表示的话，大概是这个样子。

sentences.en: And you can see that it's divided into four quadrants because there is an inner world which is mental.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它被分成四个象限，因为有一个内在世界，是心理层面的。

sentences.en: And then there's an outer world which is physical.
sentences.zh: 然后有一个外在世界，是物理层面的。

sentences.en: So by inner world, what I mean is psychological.
sentences.zh: 我说的内在世界，指的是心理层面。

sentences.en: And cultural.
sentences.zh: 以及文化层面。

sentences.en: There's your individual inner psychology, which contains your thoughts, emotions, beliefs and consciousness.
sentences.zh: 有你个体的内在心理，包含你的思想、情绪、信念和意识。

sentences.en: And then there's the collective inner world or culture which contains group beliefs, value systems and ideologies.
sentences.zh: 然后有集体的内在世界，或者说文化，包含群体信念、价值体系和意识形态。

sentences.en: Then in the outer or physical world, you have your individual outer world, which is your visible appearance, behaviors and physical brain states or other measurements.
sentences.zh: 接着在外在或物理世界里，有你个体的外在世界，也就是你可见的外表、行为和大脑的物理状态或其他测量指标。

sentences.en: And then there's the collective outer world, which is composed of systems, structures and social institutions.
sentences.zh: 然后有集体的外在世界，由系统、结构和社会制度组成。

sentences.en: Now, why does this matter?
sentences.zh: 那么，这为什么重要？

sentences.en: It's because most people and most experts only look at one of them.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人和大多数专家只看其中一个。

sentences.en: Only one quadrant.
sentences.zh: 只看一个象限。

sentences.en: The neuroscientist only sees the brain states, while the mystic only sees the vibes, or the therapist who only sees the behavior, or the sociologist who only sees the social systems, or the philosopher who only sees the meaning, which is the culture.
sentences.zh: 神经科学家只看到大脑状态，神秘主义者只看到气场，或者治疗师只看到行为，社会学家只看到社会系统，哲学家只看到意义，也就是文化。

sentences.en: So genius thinking in this context is enhanced by your ability to see all of them.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个语境下，天才思维之所以被增强，是因为你有能力看到全部。

sentences.en: So as a little example in developmental progression here, let's say that I start learning about marketing.
sentences.zh: 举一个发展进程中的小例子，假设我开始学营销。

sentences.en: I get really good at marketing.
sentences.zh: 我把营销搞得很牛。

sentences.en: And in order to do that, I have to study other people's methods. Right?
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我得研究别人的方法，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm in within one line. I'm at level one.
sentences.zh: 我处在一条线内，我在第一层。

sentences.en: I study Alex Hermosa or my own videos, and I think, oh, this is the one true way to do things.
sentences.zh: 我研究 Alex Hermosa 或者我自己的视频，然后我想，哦，这就是做事的唯一正确方法。

sentences.en: But then I grow, I become more mature.
sentences.zh: 但后来我成长了，变得更成熟了。

sentences.en: I am in the space longer and I advance to level two, and I have my own way of doing things because I've experimented so much, which has helped me learn more.
sentences.zh: 我在这个领域待得更久，进阶到了第二层，我有了自己做事的方式，因为我做了大量实验，这帮我学到了更多。

sentences.en: I become more of an expert because I'm not just copying what another person does.
sentences.zh: 我变得更像一个专家，因为我不只是在复制别人做的事。

sentences.en: I'm doing things my own way, which gives me a competitive edge.
sentences.zh: 我在用自己的方式做事，这给了我竞争优势。

sentences.en: And then if I have already pursued other interests in my life or continue pursuing interest in my life, like psychology and fitness and personal development, it gives me a deeper sense of pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 然后，如果我此前已经在生活中追求过其他兴趣，或者继续追求兴趣，比如心理学、健身和个人发展，它就会给我一种更深层的模式识别能力。

sentences.en: So not only can I understand the people that I'm working with more, or how the world works, or how culture works, and how I can apply my marketing to that thing, but it also further removes me from dogmatic thinking, which frees me up to think even more and become more creative.
sentences.zh: 所以我不光能更好地理解共事的人，或者理解世界怎么运转、文化怎么运转、我怎么把营销应用到那上面，它还能让我进一步摆脱教条式思维，这又释放出更多思考空间，让我变得更有创造力。

sentences.en: So from there, that's where things start to get interesting.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，事情才真正变得有意思起来。

sentences.en: But one thing I forgot to mention is that when you are thinking, you're usually thinking to solve a problem.
sentences.zh: 但我忘了提一件事：当你思考的时候，通常是为了解决一个问题。

sentences.en: That's what humans do.
sentences.zh: 人就是这样。

sentences.en: That's how we grow. That's what we find enjoyment in.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样成长的，也是这样找到乐趣的。

sentences.en: That's where we find growth.
sentences.zh: 我们是在那里找到成长的。

sentences.en: That's where we find development, that's progress.
sentences.zh: 我们是在那里找到发展的，那就是进步。

sentences.en: And the minute you stop growing and thus stop thinking, problems start to multiply and life just becomes considerably worse.
sentences.zh: 而一旦你停止成长、进而停止思考，问题就会开始成倍增加，生活就会变得相当糟糕。

sentences.en: So if we identify a problem in today's world, like the world is becoming corrupt and meaningless, that gives us a starting point to think right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们识别出当今世界的一个问题，比如世界正在变得腐败和毫无意义，这就给了我们一个思考的起点，对吧？

sentences.en: And it also gives us an aim for our thinking.
sentences.zh: 同时也给了我们一个思考的目标。

sentences.en: So to start thinking here, we can just question in the four perspectives or four dimensions like we talked about.
sentences.zh: 那么要在这里开始思考，我们可以像之前聊过的那样，从四个视角或者说四个维度去提问。

sentences.en: So how does society control attention and market their ideas to the masses?
sentences.zh: 社会是如何控制注意力、向大众推销他们的想法的？

sentences.en: That's the collective inner world.
sentences.zh: 这是集体的内在世界。

sentences.en: How can your behavior change more than it already has during this process?
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，你的行为怎样才能比已经发生的改变更多？

sentences.en: To have a positive impact on society?
sentences.zh: 从而对社会产生积极影响？

sentences.en: What would be the steps to reaching such a point of influence with your marketing or other things that you can leave your mark.
sentences.zh: 要达到那种影响力——通过你的营销或者其他能留下印记的东西——步骤会是什么？

sentences.en: This is the individual outer world.
sentences.zh: 这是个体的外在世界。

sentences.en: What does the job market look like right now?
sentences.zh: 现在的就业市场是什么样子？

sentences.en: Is a job an actual path to achieving such a thing?
sentences.zh: 一份工作真的是实现这种事的一条实际路径吗？

sentences.en: What about AI?
sentences.zh: AI 呢？

sentences.en: Can I utilize the technology available to me to create that impact?
sentences.zh: 我能利用现有的技术来创造那种影响吗？

sentences.en: This is the collective outer world and it's all kind of merging together. Here.
sentences.zh: 这是集体的外在世界，在这里它们全都交织在一起了。

sentences.en: Am I thinking about this the right way or is there more?
sentences.zh: 我思考这件事的方式对吗？还是说还有更多？

sentences.en: What am I missing and how does this make me feel?
sentences.zh: 我漏掉了什么？这让我感觉如何？

sentences.en: Does it make me feel motivated or inspired or hateful?
sentences.zh: 它让我感到有动力、受启发，还是充满仇恨？

sentences.en: That's the individual inner world.
sentences.zh: 这是个体的内在世界。

sentences.en: Now we can go on with that, but I think you get the point.
sentences.zh: 我们可以继续下去，但我想你明白意思了。

sentences.en: So now we get to talk about how to tap into the fifth dimension, because that was the fourth dimension.
sentences.zh: 那么现在我们可以聊聊怎么接入第五维度了，因为刚才那是第四维度。

sentences.en: But we're going to start with a quote by Krishnamurti.
sentences.zh: 但我们要从克里希那穆提的一句话开始。

sentences.en: It is no measure of health to be well-adjusted to a profoundly sick society.
sentences.zh: 适应一个病入膏肓的社会，并不是健康的标志。

sentences.en: So think about that as we go through this section.
sentences.zh: 在我们讲这一部分的时候，记住这句话。

sentences.en: In all previous examples, we never really tapped into the power of history.
sentences.zh: 在前面所有的例子里，我们从来没有真正接入历史的力量。

sentences.en: History is a very important thing, and it increases your ability to think that much more.
sentences.zh: 历史是一件非常重要的事，它能大幅提升你的思考能力。

sentences.en: Because if you understand how things develop and evolve over time, you can predict not entirely accurately, but in a more accurate way, how to go into the future, especially with your own actions, so you can set yourself up for some kind of success.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你理解事物是如何随着时间发展和演化的，你就能预测——不是完全准确，但以更准确的方式——如何走向未来，尤其是用你自己的行动，这样你就可以为某种成功做好准备。

sentences.en: But we're not trying to know here.
sentences.zh: 但我们这里不是要"知道"。

sentences.en: We're trying to understand.
sentences.zh: 我们是要"理解"。

sentences.en: We're not trying to memorize facts about certain events in history.
sentences.zh: 我们不是要记住历史上某些事件的零散事实。

sentences.en: We're trying to understand the general patterns that unfold, because that's going to allow us to understand anything that falls within those to some extent.
sentences.zh: 我们是要理解那些反复展开的通用模式，因为这样我们就能在某种程度上理解所有落入这些模式的东西。

sentences.en: So there are five things you can know here just to think about history better.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了更好地思考历史，你需要知道五件事。

sentences.en: And we're going to just run through these because I want to leave you to thinking on your own.
sentences.zh: 我们快速过一遍，因为我想把思考的空间留给你自己。

sentences.en: The first thing is that the master pattern is transcendent.
sentences.zh: 第一件事：元模式是超越的。

sentences.en: Include.
sentences.zh: 并且包含。

sentences.en: So if you take a materialist, he would say that reality is composed of atoms.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个唯物主义者，他会说现实由原子构成。

sentences.en: If you take a mentalist, then he would say that reality is composed of qualia.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个唯心主义者，他会说现实由感受质构成。

sentences.en: But if we zoom out for the sake of understanding, we understand that they're both correct because they're in separate perspectives.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们为了理解而把镜头拉远，就会明白两者都对，因为他们只是站在不同的视角。

sentences.en: So if we look at what's actually happening throughout history, we can understand that reality is composed on a very general and metaphorical level of whole parts.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们观察历史上实际发生的事情，就能理解，在一个非常概括和隐喻的层面上，现实是由"整体/部分"构成的。

sentences.en: What that means is that it's composed of holes, but those holes are also parts.
sentences.zh: 意思是说，它由整体构成，但这些整体同时也是部分。

sentences.en: As some examples, matter evolves into life evolves into mind.
sentences.zh: 举个例子：物质进化为生命，生命进化为心智。

sentences.en: Each of those are a whole.
sentences.zh: 每一个都是一个整体。

sentences.en: And so like matter is a part of life, but it's also a whole in itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，物质是生命的一部分，但它本身也是一个整体。

sentences.en: Then you can think of word to sentence to paragraph to chapter, to book, to library, to wherever you want to go.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以去想：词到句子到段落到章节到书到图书馆，一直推到你想到达的任何地方。

sentences.en: Then you have machine to computer, to artificial intelligence, to whatever comes after that, or you have human to house to city, to state to country, to continent to planet, to solar system, to galaxy, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 然后是机器到计算机到人工智能到之后出现的任何东西，或者人到房屋到城市到州到国家到大陆到行星到太阳系到银河系，以此类推。

sentences.en: This is why everything is connected in the way that people talk about is because when you observe reality from a broad enough level, you see exactly this.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们常说万物相连——当你从一个足够宽广的层面观察现实，你看到的就是这个。

sentences.en: So with each evolution of something, when something new emerges, it transcends and includes the thing before it.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着事物的每一次进化，当新东西涌现出来，它会超越并包含它之前的东西。

sentences.en: What that means, the important thing there is that if you transcend and you don't include, then something's wrong.
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？重要的是：如果你超越了却没有包含，那就出问题了。

sentences.en: And if you remove one of the parts from the whole that allowed that thing to exist, then the whole self-destructs.
sentences.zh: 而如果你把让某个事物得以存在的部分从整体中移除，这个整体就会自我毁灭。

sentences.en: So this is why environmentalists are so concerned with climate change is because if the biosphere goes to crap, then humanity goes down with it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么环保主义者如此关注气候变化——因为如果生物圈完蛋了，人类也会跟着完蛋。

sentences.en: But then you look at it from a technologist point of view and they're like, well, we don't really care about the environment right now because we're eventually going to create the technology that allows us to make the biosphere better, and it will survive that way.
sentences.zh: 但你从技术主义者的视角看，他们会说，我们现在其实不太在乎环境，因为我们最终会创造出能让生物圈变得更好的技术，它会以那种方式存活下来。

sentences.en: So they're thinking in terms of acceleration and progress while the environmentalist are thinking of not necessarily regression, but doing things differently right now so that we can slow down the use of the resources that would make the biosphere bad.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在用加速和进步的思维思考，而环保主义者想的未必是倒退，而是现在就换一种方式做事，好让我们放慢对资源的消耗，避免把生物圈搞砸。

sentences.en: Now, this will make more sense with examples.
sentences.zh: 好，这些用例子讲会更清楚。

sentences.en: So the second thing you need to know is just how individuals evolve physically. Right.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要知道的第二件事，就是个体如何在物理层面进化。

sentences.en: So we need to cover how individuals evolve physically and mentally.
sentences.zh: 我们需要讲个体如何在物理层面和心理层面进化。

sentences.en: Then how collectives evolve physically and mentally.
sentences.zh: 然后讲集体如何在物理层面和心理层面进化。

sentences.en: Humans specifically tend to evolve or develop through an increasing circle of care or concern.
sentences.zh: 人类，具体来说，倾向于通过一个不断扩大的关怀圈来进化或发展。

sentences.en: So it goes from egocentric to ethnocentric to world centric to cosmos centric or reality itself.
sentences.zh: 所以它从自我中心到族群中心到世界中心到宇宙中心或现实本身。

sentences.en: What that means is that you're born and you kind of start out selfish, and then you identify with your tribe or your group, and then you identify with humanity as a whole or the world, and then so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 意思是说，你出生时一开始是自私的，然后你认同你的部落或群体，然后你认同整个人类或世界，然后以此类推。

sentences.en: But the thing here is that people try to skip levels they don't understand, transcend and include.
sentences.zh: 但这里的问题是，人们试图跳过某些层次——他们不理解"超越并包含"。

sentences.en: They try to identify as this world centric person who just cares about everyone's equality, but they don't understand that you also have to care about your group and yourself, because those heavily impact how much you can care about the world.
sentences.zh: 他们试图把自己标榜成一个世界中心的人，只关心所有人的平等，但他们不明白，你也必须关心你的群体和你自己，因为这些会严重影响你能在多大程度上关心世界。

sentences.en: It's like you can't. What's the fricking what's the quote where you can't fill someone's glass from if your own is empty?
sentences.zh: 就好像你做不到。那句话怎么说的来着？自己的杯子是空的，就没法给别人倒水。

sentences.en: So this has to be accounted for in your thinking, because these people who identify as these world centric, virtuous people are smart but dumb.
sentences.zh: 所以你在思考时必须把这一点考虑进去，因为那些自诩为世界中心、道德高尚的人，其实是聪明反被聪明误。

sentences.en: You do not sacrifice your own values or your group values for the sake of these world values.
sentences.zh: 你不能为了这些世界层面的价值观，去牺牲你自己的价值观或你所在群体的价值观。

sentences.en: That sounds so noble when it doesn't work without the latter.
sentences.zh: 这话听起来特别高尚，但如果没有后者，根本行不通。

sentences.en: I mean the former.
sentences.zh: 我是说前者。

sentences.en: Sorry, I can't remember if I preface that as individuals evolving physically or mentally, but that was obviously mentally right.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不记得我开头说的是个体在身体上进化还是在精神上进化，但显然是指精神上的，对吧。

sentences.en: Your circle of concern.
sentences.zh: 你的关切圈。

sentences.en: Physically, it's pretty obvious.
sentences.zh: 身体层面，这很明显。

sentences.en: You go from atom to cell to molecule to organism, and you can like, see and feel and taste and touch the physical world.
sentences.zh: 你从原子到细胞到分子到有机体，你能看到、感觉到、尝到、触摸到物理世界。

sentences.en: You understand how this happens now in terms of how societies evolve physically and mentally.
sentences.zh: 你现在理解了社会是如何在身体和精神上演化的。

sentences.en: They're both deeply intertwined because the tools allow for the worldview or the value system to emerge.
sentences.zh: 这两者深度交织，因为工具让世界观或价值体系得以涌现。

sentences.en: Now physically in societies, we see that people evolved from tribes to villages to empires to nation states.
sentences.zh: 在社会身体层面的演化中，我们看到人类从部落到村庄到帝国再到民族国家。

sentences.en: And the technology here was first hunting and gathering with simple tools and then digging sticks and hoes, which enabled some food surplus.
sentences.zh: 这里的技术，首先是使用简单工具的狩猎采集，然后是挖掘棍和锄头，这带来了少量的食物盈余。

sentences.en: And then we invented the horse drawn plow, which led to even more of a food surplus that allowed people to discover and explore and conquer.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发明了马拉犁，带来了更多的食物盈余，让人们能够去发现、探索和征服。

sentences.en: This is close to the enlightenment and why that happened.
sentences.zh: 这很接近启蒙运动及其发生的原因。

sentences.en: But then we invented machines and computers, and we abstracted ourselves further away from both human labor and animal labor.
sentences.zh: 但接着我们发明了机器和计算机，我们把自己从人力和畜力中进一步抽象出来。

sentences.en: So the evolution of societies physically allowed for them to evolve mentally as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，社会在身体层面的演化，也允许了它们在精神层面的演化。

sentences.en: And this happens in a similar way as it does in individuals where it's egocentric, ethnocentric, world centric.
sentences.zh: 这跟个体的演化方式很相似，都是从自我中心，到族群中心，再到世界中心。

sentences.en: But when we are talking about societies or collectives, it helps to use different terminology.
sentences.zh: 但当我们谈论社会或集体时，用不同的术语会更有帮助。

sentences.en: So we can use something like pre-modern modern to postmodern or pre rational to rational, to post rational and then trans rational.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以用前现代、现代、后现代，或者前理性、理性、后理性，再到超理性这样的说法。

sentences.en: But what that means is that in earlier societies we first conformed to authority, right?
sentences.zh: 但这意味着，在早期社会，我们首先服从于权威，对吧？

sentences.en: All we believed was that there were rain gods in the sky, and if it rained, we made them happy.
sentences.zh: 我们相信的只是天上有雨神，如果下雨了，就是我们让他们高兴了。

sentences.en: And then we discovered science and reason, and we started to value progress.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现了科学和理性，我们开始重视进步。

sentences.en: And now we're in this post-modern world where we kind of deconstruct everything, and we think everything should be equal when it doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 现在我们身处这个后现代世界，我们解构一切，认为一切都应该平等，但现实并非如此运作。

sentences.en: And so we need to transcend and include the good parts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要超越并包容其中好的部分。

sentences.en: So if we ground this and make this practical and how to actually think about it, think of where we are right now in the age of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们把这个落到实处，让它变得实用，讲讲到底该怎么思考，想想我们现在所处的智能时代。

sentences.en: If you are still operating on industrial age technology as a business or you think that the right path to go down is go to school, get a job, retire at 65, because that's what you would do in the industrial age.
sentences.zh: 如果你作为一家企业，还在用工业时代的技术运作，或者你认为正确的道路是上学、找工作、65岁退休，因为那是你在工业时代会做的事。

sentences.en: You're running on this outdated software and you need to change it.
sentences.zh: 你就是在运行这套过时的软件，你需要改变它。

sentences.en: So if we want to make this practical, we want to grounded.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们想让它变得实用，我们想让它落地。

sentences.en: We can think of the situation we're currently in, where AI is on our doorstep and no one knows what to do next, right?
sentences.zh: 我们可以想想我们当前的处境，AI 已经近在眼前，没人知道下一步该怎么办，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the biggest problem.
sentences.zh: 这是最大的问题。

sentences.en: But if we look back at history, we can at least tell whether what we're doing is good or not, or is going to be beneficial for the future.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们回顾历史，我们至少能判断我们正在做的事是好是坏，或者对未来是否有益。

sentences.en: So if you're still running on industrial technology as a business, then that's probably not a smart thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你作为一家企业，还在用工业时代的技术运作，那可能不是个聪明的做法。

sentences.en: If you aren't integrating AI in some way, transcending including, then you're probably falling behind.
sentences.zh: 如果你不以某种方式整合 AI，去超越并包容，那你很可能正在落后。

sentences.en: And if you as an individual still have the default plan of the industrial age to go to school, get a job, retire at 65 when jobs are at threat of automation and you can't think creatively of as to what you can do, or you can't predict, at least somewhat accurately, what a good path to go down is.
sentences.zh: 如果你作为一个个体，仍然抱着工业时代的默认计划——上学、找工作、65岁退休——而工作正面临自动化的威胁，你又无法创造性地思考自己能做什么，或者无法至少在一定程度上准确预判哪条路值得走。

sentences.en: That's how this is practical.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的实用之处。

sentences.en: That's what I talk about in like all of my videos now, everything I say obviously isn't going to be correct, but I do think it's heading in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 我现在几乎每期视频都在讲这个，我说的所有东西显然不可能全对，但我确实认为大方向是对的。

sentences.en: I'm open to being wrong, but I'm also putting out there.
sentences.zh: 我接受自己可能犯错，但我依然会把它说出来。

sentences.en: I'm not just telling people to sit around and just be bulldozed over.
sentences.zh: 我不是在告诉人们坐着等死、任人碾压。

sentences.en: Now, another practical way to think about this is when you're engaging in debate with another person or on social media, you can start to identify where they lie and what type of thinking they're using.
sentences.zh: 另一个实用的思考角度是，当你和别人辩论，或者在社交媒体上跟人交锋时，你可以开始识别他们处在哪个层次、在使用哪种思维方式。

sentences.en: So if you're on social media and someone's just being super polarizing or dogmatic or whatever it may be, you can assume that they're thinking stupidly and they're just trying to defend their own beliefs.
sentences.zh: 如果你在社交媒体上看到有人特别极端、特别教条，不管是什么表现，你可以判断他们是在愚蠢地思考，只是在捍卫自己的信念。

sentences.en: Or if they sound like a TV or social media itself or the news, you can assume that they're just regurgitating this preprogramed line of thought.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果他们说话像电视、像社交媒体本身、像新闻，你可以判断他们只是在复读这些预设好的思路。

sentences.en: They're not thinking at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有在思考。

sentences.en: Now, the most useful thing here is to just identify where you are at, where your own center of gravity is, so that you can identify your own blind spots and see past them.
sentences.zh: 这里最有用的，就是识别你自己处在哪个位置，你自己的重心在哪里，这样你才能发现自己的盲点，并看穿它们。

sentences.en: You don't need to compete with someone else on how well you can think.
sentences.zh: 你不需要跟别人比谁更会思考。

sentences.en: You simply need to think better.
sentences.zh: 你只需要让自己思考得更好。

sentences.en: So we've covered a lot of frameworks.
sentences.zh: 我们讲了很多框架。

sentences.en: We've tapped into this fifth dimensional thinking, but we missed something pretty important here.
sentences.zh: 我们已经触及了这种五维思考，但我们漏掉了一个相当重要的东西。

sentences.en: We missed the main thing because stupid thinking is just when you stop thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们漏掉了核心，因为愚蠢的思考，就是你停止思考的那一刻。

sentences.en: But what makes a person stop thinking?
sentences.zh: 但什么会让一个人停止思考？

sentences.en: What makes them turn in on themselves and to just start defending themselves endlessly?
sentences.zh: 什么会让他们封闭自己，开始无休止地自我辩护？

sentences.en: The answer here is identity and you latching on to beliefs, ideas or constructs and just making them a part of who you are because that's inherently limiting.
sentences.zh: 答案是身份认同，是你死死抓住某些信念、想法或建构，把它们变成你自我的一部分，因为这本身就是一种限制。

sentences.en: Especially if those ideas, beliefs, or constructs are small, right?
sentences.zh: 尤其是当这些想法、信念或建构本身就很狭隘的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: Your your ability to think is determined by your world model.
sentences.zh: 你的思考能力，是由你的世界模型决定的。

sentences.en: It's determined by your beliefs.
sentences.zh: 是由你的信念决定的。

sentences.en: So you should, in my opinion, adopt the most encompassing world model that you can if you willingly adopt something going into it, knowing that it's dogmatic, that it's ideological, that it's very one dimensional, then you're going to, you're thinking, is going to take the shape of that.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，你应该主动去采纳你能找到的最具包容性的世界模型。如果你明知某个东西是教条的、意识形态化的、非常单一维度的，还自愿跳进去，那你的思考也会被塑造成那个形状。

sentences.en: Think of the diehard Republicans or Democrats, right?
sentences.zh: 想想那些死忠的共和党人或民主党人，对吧？

sentences.en: If you become one of the diehards, then you can't think out of that little bubble.
sentences.zh: 如果你成了死忠之一，你就无法跳出那个小泡泡去思考。

sentences.en: Therefore, you will never be able to find the truth of the situation.
sentences.zh: 因此，你永远无法找到事情的真相。

sentences.en: You're just going to be arguing in circles and going nowhere.
sentences.zh: 你只会在原地绕圈争论，哪里也到不了。

sentences.en: I don't know how more people don't see that or realize it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么还有那么多人看不出来、意识不到这一点。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that you can't adopt the values of either side, or think that certain sides hold certain truths.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你不能采纳任何一方的价值观，或者认为某一方掌握了某些真理。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that you have to turn against both of them.
sentences.zh: 也不意味着你必须跟两边都对着干。

sentences.en: That's not how this works either.
sentences.zh: 也不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: It simply means that you don't need to feel threatened when someone else disagrees with you, because that threat is signaling that you think you that's who you are.
sentences.zh: 它只是意味着，当别人不同意你的时候，你不需要感到被威胁，因为那种威胁感在告诉你，你把那个观点当成了你自己。

sentences.en: Now, this isn't only in politics.
sentences.zh: 这不只存在于政治领域。

sentences.en: This is literally every single domain, even something as small as marketing, like we talked about earlier, you wouldn't know the amount of times that I've seen people on the internet talk about, let's say, Alex or Moses methods, and then someone disagrees with them and says that there can be a better way, and then they just argue endlessly.
sentences.zh: 这存在于每一个领域，哪怕是像营销这么小的事，就像我们之前聊过的。你不知道我在网上见过多少次，人们讨论比如 Alex 或 Moses 的方法，然后有人不同意，说有更好的方式，接着他们就无休止地争吵。

sentences.en: It's like, how can you not how can you not see that it applies to religion, it applies to vocation. It it applies to everything.
sentences.zh: 就好像，你怎么能看不出来，这同样适用于宗教，适用于职业，适用于一切。

sentences.en: So a helpful thing here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个很有用的东西。

sentences.en: And another thing to think about is how you came about getting these beliefs.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事值得思考：你这些信念是怎么来的。

sentences.en: Because most people in today's world haven't thought an original thought a single day in their life.
sentences.zh: 因为当今世界的大多数人，一辈子都没产生过一个属于自己的想法。

sentences.en: You were born into a specific part of the world.
sentences.zh: 你出生在世界的某个特定角落。

sentences.en: That specific part of the world is called a culture.
sentences.zh: 那个特定角落叫文化。

sentences.en: That culture is practically holds its own value system and belief system.
sentences.zh: 那个文化本质上承载着自己的一套价值体系和信念体系。

sentences.en: If your parents were raised in that culture and you were raised by your parents, those were probably imposed on you.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母在那个文化中长大，而你由父母养大，这些东西很可能被强加到了你身上。

sentences.en: And since you weren't able to think for yourself, you adopted them for the sake of survival because you have to survive, or else you'll be kicked out of the house or something worse.
sentences.zh: 而因为你当时还无法独立思考，你为了生存接受了它们——你必须活下去，否则就会被赶出家门，或者更糟。

sentences.en: I mean, even in another part of the world with a different value system, you could literally get killed and you don't want that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在世界的另一个地方，有着不同的价值体系，你甚至可能真的被杀掉，你当然不想那样。

sentences.en: So you conform, you start at level one.
sentences.zh: 所以你顺从了，你从第一层开始。

sentences.en: And so those beliefs limit how far you can think from the get go.
sentences.zh: 于是这些信念从一开始就限制了你思考的边界。

sentences.en: And most people don't ever question that.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人从未质疑过这一点。

sentences.en: They never break out of that bubble.
sentences.zh: 他们从未打破那个泡泡。

sentences.en: That is the greatest trap you can fall into because you have to remember your mind is how you interact with reality.
sentences.zh: 这是你能掉入的最大陷阱，因为你必须记住，你的心智是你与现实互动的方式。

sentences.en: Remember, you see information, you interpret it or make sense of it at your current level line altitude of thinking.
sentences.zh: 记住，你看到信息，在你当前的思考高度上解读它、理解它。

sentences.en: And then you make a choice, and then you do that again and again and again, and then it crystallizes.
sentences.zh: 然后你做出一个选择，然后你一次又一次地重复，然后它就固化了。

sentences.en: It becomes conditioned, it becomes repetitive robotic, and it determines the outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 它变成了条件反射，变成了重复的、机械的，然后它决定了你人生的结果。

sentences.en: That's insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So you have to increase the space.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须扩大那个空间。

sentences.en: You have to expand how many perspectives you can hold.
sentences.zh: 你必须扩展你能容纳的视角数量。

sentences.en: You have to be able to navigate multiple different scenarios.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够驾驭多种不同的情境。

sentences.en: If you only think within the confines set by your parents, teachers, employers, and peers on social media, the outcome of your life isn't going to be pretty.
sentences.zh: 如果你只在父母、老师、老板和社交媒体上的同龄人设定的边界内思考，你人生的结局不会好看。

sentences.en: Just observe where the average person ends up and it's not hard to see that.
sentences.zh: 只要观察一下普通人最终走到了哪里，这不难看到。

sentences.en: So the next time you feel questioned, I beg of you, this is the only thing you have to do is just pause, look at it, observe how you feel and do not collapse in on yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以下次你感到被质疑的时候，我恳求你，你唯一需要做的就是暂停，看着它，观察你的感受，不要向内崩塌。

sentences.en: Just allow it to sit there, right?
sentences.zh: 就让它待在那里，好吗？

sentences.en: Just don't respond.

sentences.en: Just let it pass by and see where that takes you.
